The diagram shows an object released from point X and travelling on a frictionless track. If a heavier object is taken in consideration then:

(The figure shows a frictionless track. Point X is at a height of 25 m, point Y at 15 m, the bottom of the valley Z is at ground level, point M is the top of a hump at 20 m, and point N is at 10 m. The object is released from rest at X and slides along the curved track X → Y → Z → M → N.)

Consider the following statements:
(i) It will move with a greater speed at Y.
(ii) The speed of the object at M is 10 m s⁻¹.

Two activities are performed with the same solid iron cuboid placed on loose sand: in activity (i) the cuboid stands in an upright position (resting on its smallest face, the small base touching the sand), and in activity (ii) the same cuboid lies flat (resting on its largest face). In the activity shown, more impression will be made by the cuboid in the sand in case of:

options.label: B
options.text: neither in activity (i) nor in activity (ii)

stem:
Two activities (i) and (ii) are performed by a student for comparing the pressure exerted by solid iron cuboids having the same weight and dimensions on loose sand.

(The figure shows two set-ups on loose sand. In Activity (i) the cuboid stands upright, resting on its small base, so it sinks deep into the sand. In Activity (ii) an identical cuboid lies flat on its large face, resting on a much larger contact area, so it barely sinks.)

If P₁ and P₂ are the pressures exerted by the set-up in the two activities respectively, then the observation made by her is:
An iceberg floats with ______ of its volume below ______.
